candidates.title: Palette Collision Checker
candidates.plainSentence: A checker that lets you paste chart colours and see which pairs look alike to colour-blind viewers, then nudges them apart.
candidates.pitch: Paste the 3 to 8 colours of a chart or a brand palette and the page shows, for every pair, the worst-case perceptual distance across normal vision and three kinds of colour blindness, as a head-to-head matrix with the numbers shown. Pairs that collapse are flagged in red; one button nudges only the offending colours by the smallest lightness and chroma change until every pair clears a threshold you can set, and the result exports as hex and CSS variables. Everything runs in the browser, nothing is uploaded.
candidates.firstMinute: The page opens with a sample 6-colour chart palette already analysed: a strip of swatches, the same strip as seen with red-green and blue-yellow colour blindness, and a pair matrix where two cells glow red because those colours merge. Pressing Fix turns the red cells green and shows what changed in each colour, with no reading needed. Pasting your own hex codes replaces the sample instantly.
conceptsToLearn: Some people cannot tell apart colours that look clearly different to others, so a chart needs colours that differ in lightness as well as hue
candidates.whyNow: Timeless: every dashboard and chart needs a categorical palette, and colour-blindness checks are usually done by eye on a screenshot. Not news-bound.

purposeDetail.job: Find the colour pairs in a palette that become indistinguishable under colour-vision deficiency, show the measured distance for each pair, and repair them with the smallest change.
purposeDetail.audience: Designers, analysts and developers who pick colours for charts, maps, UI states and brand palettes and have no quick way to test them beyond eyeballing a simulator.

paywallEvidence.product: A design-plugin accessibility suite (colour-blindness simulator and contrast checker)
paywallEvidence.whatIsGated: Reportedly the free tier simulates 3 deficiency types and the paid tier all 8, at about 15 USD a month; from older vendor material and one review, unconfirmed for today

purposeDetail.freeGap: Free options already simulate colour blindness and flag look-alike colours (a free palette evaluator does this and exports values). The remaining gap is a private, offline page that shows its working as a pair-by-pair distance table, tests against all three dichromacies at once, checks each colour against a chosen background, and proposes a minimal repair instead of leaving the fix to the visitor. The page must not claim to replace any of them, and the paywall claim is unverified and never reaches the page.
purposeDetail.oracle: The supplementary CIEDE2000 test data of Sharma, Wu and Dalal (2005), published by the first author as plain-text rows of reference and sample CIELAB values with the expected colour difference; plus the colour-vision-deficiency matrices of Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes (2009).
purposeDetail.inputs: 3 to 8 hex colours (typed, pasted from a list, or picked), an optional background colour, a distance threshold.
purposeDetail.outputs: A pair matrix of worst-case colour difference, simulated strips for normal vision, protan, deutan and tritan, contrast ratio against the background, a repaired palette; exports as a hex list, CSS custom properties and a PNG strip.
purposeDetail.limits: Simulations are models of full dichromacy, not of every person; there is no accepted universal distance threshold, so the default is a labelled convention; it does not test text legibility, patterns or shape cues, and is a screening aid, not a certification.

research.summary: Colour-difference maths is standardised and testable: CIEDE2000 has a published supplementary test set by Sharma, Wu and Dalal that exposes common implementation errors, and the Machado et al. 2009 model supplies the colour-vision-deficiency matrices that open-source libraries reuse. Free palette evaluators exist (one flags look-alike colours under simulated deficiencies), so the idea wins on being private, offline, numeric and repairing, not on novelty of the simulator. No published minimum distance for colour-blind-safe categorical palettes was found; the threshold is a convention and the page says so. Fetching pages failed, so all evidence is from search results.

sources.title: The CIEDE2000 (Gaurav Sharma, University of Rochester)
sources.snippet: The author's page offers test data for checking CIEDE2000 software: plain-text rows of reference and sample CIELAB values with the expected difference, a spreadsheet and a MATLAB program. It says it is not an official CIE implementation.
sources.note: Primary source of the known-answer test data; the Sharma, Wu, Dalal paper is Color Research and Application 30, 2005, pp. 21-30.

sources.title: Validation of CIEDE2000 color-difference formula implementation using test data from Sharma, Wu & Dalal
sources.snippet: A third-party notebook loads the paper's table of pairs with intermediate terms and final colour differences and compares an implementation against them.
sources.note: Independent confirmation that the table exists and is used to validate implementations.

sources.title: CVD Simulation (Oliveira, UFRGS)
sources.snippet: The authors' page for the 2009 physiologically-based model of colour-vision-deficiency simulation (IEEE TVCG 15(6), pp. 1291-1298) covering dichromacy and anomalous trichromacy.
sources.note: Primary source of the simulation model; matrix coefficients were not visible in the result.

sources.title: Source code for colour.blindness.machado2009 (colour-science docs)
sources.snippet: An open-source colour library implements the Machado 2009 model as a function that returns the deficiency matrix.
sources.note: Independent evidence the model is a standard, reusable method.

sources.title: Viz Palette Helps You Pick Colors for Your Maps and Data Visualizations (Geography Realm)
sources.snippet: Describes a free palette tool by two visualization practitioners that switches between colour-deficiency views, marks colours that are hard to tell apart with arcs and exports hex, RGB or HSL.
sources.note: Shows free options exist; defines the freeGap honestly.

sources.title: Viz Palette for Data Visualization Color (Towards Data Science)
sources.snippet: One of the tool authors describes it as a way to evaluate and improve palettes, including similar-colour reports.
sources.note: Second, independent description of the free tool.

sources.title: Announcing Stark's Paid Plans (Stark blog)
sources.snippet: Vendor blog post announcing paid plans for designers and teams; the snippet did not show which features sit behind them.
sources.note: Establishes paid plans exist; the split of simulator types came only from a blended summary and an old archived pricing page.

sources.title: Stark review (Who Is Accessible)
sources.snippet: A review lists a limited free plan and a Pro plan at about 15 USD per month with extra checks, and a cheaper team tier.
sources.note: Third-party pricing; undated here and not confirmed by the vendor's current pricing page.

sources.title: palettecore: Derive, optimise and audit a scientific colour palette from one seed colour
sources.snippet: A package maximises the smallest pairwise colour difference across normal vision and three simulated deficiencies, and states its thresholds are configurable design rules, not accessibility standards.
sources.note: Supports the maximin repair idea and the absence of a standard threshold.

sources.title: Oklab color space
sources.snippet: Background: Oklab was introduced in December 2020, is defined relative to D65 XYZ, and appears in CSS Color 4 and 5 drafts.
sources.note: Basis for doing the repair in a perceptual space; exact matrix values still to be taken from the author's own post.

facts.claim: Sharma, Wu and Dalal (2005) published supplementary CIEDE2000 test data, as rows of reference and sample CIELAB values with the expected colour difference, because the original sample data does not expose several implementation errors.
Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes (2009, IEEE TVCG 15(6) 1291-1298) give a model for simulating protan, deutan and tritan vision that open-source libraries implement as deficiency matrices.
A free palette-evaluation tool (Viz Palette) already simulates colour-vision deficiencies, flags hard-to-distinguish colours and exports hex, RGB or HSL values, so a simulator alone is not a gap.

As of 2026-10-13, per older vendor material and one review: a design-plugin suite reportedly offers a 3-type colour-blindness simulator free and all 8 types on a paid plan around 15 USD a month. Not confirmed on the vendor's current pricing page.
No published minimum CIEDE2000 distance for colour-blind-safe categorical palettes was found; one package describes its thresholds as configurable design rules.
Oklab, introduced by Bjorn Ottosson in December 2020, was fitted to correct hue and lightness shifts in blues seen in CIELAB and appears in CSS Color drafts.

design.coreLoop: Paste or edit colours, read the pair matrix where each cell is a head-to-head between two colours, press Fix on the red cells, compare before and after strips, tune the threshold and background, export. It stays interesting because each edit moves the numbers instantly and the repair shows exactly which colour moved and by how much.
sophisticationHooks: Worst-case CIEDE2000 across normal, protan, deutan and tritan views, shown as numbers in a matrix
Minimal repair that moves only offending colours in a perceptual space and prints before and after values
Self-test panel that runs the published CIEDE2000 test rows and lists pass or fail
Contrast ratio of each colour against a chosen background
design.scopeForOneDay: Built: hex parser, sRGB to linear, three simulation matrices, CIELAB and CIEDE2000, pair matrix, greedy maximin repair in OKLCH, swatch strips, hex/CSS/PNG export, self-test with the test rows. Cut: image upload, anomalous trichromacy severities, saved palettes, text-legibility checks.
risks: The 3x3 simulation matrices and the CIEDE2000 test rows were not visible in search results (fetching failed); the builder must take them from the published paper or the author's file and cite them, otherwise the oracle is only a regression check.
The Stark pricing split is unverified and is not shown on the page; the page never names any product.
No standard distance threshold exists; the page labels its default (a convention) and lets the visitor change it.
Free tools overlap; the pitch rests on private, offline, numeric and repairing, not on novelty.
Simulation applies in linear RGB; mistakes there silently skew results, so the self-test must cover the simulator too.

candidates.title: How Letters Get Spaced
candidates.plainSentence: A lesson that shows, with draggable letters, how type designers space letters by equalising white area and when a pair still needs kerning.
candidates.pitch: Start by fixing an ugly word with a tracking slider and one kerning drag, then discover why the same distance between letter edges looks different for HH, HO and AV: what the eye reads is the white area. A ladder of small demos built on a typeface drawn in code lets the visitor space letters by area, watch the rhythm of a row of n and o, blur the text to see its grey tone, and learn which pairs spacing cannot fix.
candidates.firstMinute: The page opens on the word AVOID set with default spacing, with the gap between A and V shaded so the hole is visible, and a tracking slider plus a draggable pair handle. Dragging the V towards the A closes the hole and the shaded area number drops, which is the first success with no reading.
conceptsToLearn: Every letter sits in a box with a little space on each side; the gap you see between two letters is the sum of those two spaces
candidates.whyNow: Timeless: anyone who sets headlines, logos or slides meets uneven letter gaps. Type spacing is a niche most people have never been shown properly.

purposeDetail.concept: Letter spacing is set by the white area between letters, not by the distance between their edges; kerning is a patch for the few pairs that spacing cannot fix.
purposeDetail.whyNiche: People know the words kerning and tracking but rarely see how a type designer sets the space on each side of every letter first, or why diagonal and round letters break the rules.
purposeDetail.audience: Designers, students, slide-makers and curious readers; no design knowledge needed.
misconceptions: Kerning and tracking are the same thing.
Uneven spacing is fixed by adding kerning pairs everywhere.
purposeDetail.ahaMoment: Two pairs with identical edge-to-edge distance, H next to H and A next to V, look nothing alike, and the shaded white areas show why; closing the area, not the distance, evens the row.
demos: 1. Tracking against kerning: a slider moves every gap, a handle moves one pair.
2. Same distance, different area: shaded gaps for HH, HO, OO and AV with live area numbers.
3. Space by area: set one target area and see sidebearings computed for a small geometric typeface drawn from shapes, with an n-and-o rhythm strip.
4. Blur test: a squint slider shows the grey tone of a line before and after spacing.
5. What spacing cannot fix: AV, To and WA, where a hand-set kerning pair is the right tool.
checkQuestions: If you tighten every gap in a headline equally, are you tracking or kerning?
Which pair needs more care at equal edge distance: HH or AV, and why?
After spacing by area, one pair still looks open. What is the right fix?

research.summary: The lesson rests on how type designers space fonts. Foundry guidance says to fix spacing through each glyph's side spaces first and use kerning only for pairs that remain awkward. Spacing guides describe judging letters against a fence of n or m and aiming for an even grey tone. An open area-based spacing script equalises the white area and depth per letter group but does not kern and does not replace the eye. Kerning and tracking are widely confused. The typeface will be drawn in code from shapes, so no font file is used. Page fetching failed, so everything is from search results.

sources.title: Bad Spacing (Monotype Foundry Support)
sources.snippet: Foundry guidance: spacing problems are not to be solved with kerning pairs; set each glyph's sidebearings first, then add kerning for specific exceptions; a round o should sit centred in its space.
sources.note: Primary-domain statement of the sidebearings-first order.

sources.title: FontLab TV: spacing letters from scratch
sources.snippet: Advises solving spacing with sidebearings wherever possible and reserving kerning for pairs nothing else can fix.
sources.note: Independent second source for the order of work.

sources.title: The Briem method and the geometry of nothing (FontLab blog)
sources.snippet: Treats spacing as setting rhythm and describes linking sidebearings of related letters to the n.
sources.note: Control-letter method and rhythm.

sources.title: Leiden University thesis on letter spacing
sources.snippet: States that type designers often start with a fence of n or m and judge other letters against it, and that only the x-height zone matters for spacing roman lowercase.
sources.note: Academic support for the n-fence and the x-height zone.

sources.title: A free tool for spacing fonts (HT Letterspacer)
sources.snippet: An open spacing tool sets sidebearings from the white area and depth of each glyph; it does not kern and does not replace the eye of an experienced designer.
sources.note: Area-and-depth method and its stated limits; the tool's own page.

sources.title: Class 4 - Controlling Space, Leading, Tracking and Kerning (CUNY City Tech course)
sources.snippet: A design course page that treats kerning as pair adjustment and notes it is often confused with tracking.
sources.note: Documents the misconception; the search summary attributing this was blended.

sources.title: Adventures in Space: Tracking (FontShop article on MyFonts)
sources.snippet: Says the two terms are frequently confused; kerning fixes a specific pair, tracking spaces a run of text as a design choice.
sources.note: Definitions and the confusion; many language copies of one article count once.

sources.title: Kerning glossary (unicodefyi)
sources.snippet: Explains that a letter's bounding box ignores its shape, so diagonal and round letters leave uneven gaps, with A-V, T-o and W-A as typical problem pairs.
sources.note: Why box-to-box spacing fails; many language copies count once.

sources.title: Journal of Graphic Engineering and Design paper on letterspacing
sources.snippet: States the goal as letters that look equally distant within words and paragraphs, giving an even value of grey without darker or lighter patches.
sources.note: Supports the even-grey goal and the blur test.

sources.title: Adventures in Space: Kerning (FontShop article on MyFonts)
sources.snippet: Search summary said sidebearings handle most issues but letters such as A, L, T, V, W and Y trap space so some pairs need kerning.
sources.note: Seen only in a blended summary, so lower confidence.

facts.claim: Kerning adjusts the space of one specific letter pair; tracking (also called letter-spacing) changes the spacing of a whole run of text.
Kerning and tracking are frequently confused with each other.
Foundry guidance says spacing problems should not be fixed by adding kerning pairs: set sidebearings first, then kern the exceptions.
Type designers commonly judge spacing against a fence of n or m letters and aim for an even grey value; only the x-height zone matters for roman lowercase.
An open area-based spacing tool equalises the white area and depth of letters per group, does not kern, and does not replace a designer's eye.
A letter's bounding box ignores its shape, so diagonal and round letters (A-V, T-o, W-A) leave uneven gaps that need kerning.

design.coreLoop: Demo, question, aha: see a flaw, move a handle or slider to remove it, read the number that changes, then answer a check question whose answer follows from the same model; each rung adds one idea.
sophisticationHooks: A geometric typeface of about 12 letters drawn in code from rectangles, circles and polygons, so area is computed exactly and no font file is used
Live white-area readout between neighbours inside the x-height zone, capped by depth
Blur slider to see grey tone before and after spacing
Kerning pair editor that shows when area equalisation has run out
design.scopeForOneDay: Built: glyph set as SVG paths, area-between-glyphs routine (raster on an offscreen canvas, fixed resolution), five demos, three check questions with computed answers, intro and glossary. Cut: real font loading, full alphabet, export of a font, language-specific rules.
risks: Area equalisation is a simplified model of a judgement-based craft; the page must say it is a model and that real fonts are finished by eye.
Kerning and tracking confusion is documented by a course page and a FontShop article, but the summary attributing it was blended, so the page words it as widely reported.
The A-L-T-V-W-Y claim was seen only in a blended summary and is not stated as fact.
The page must not name tools or foundries as endorsements; the method is described in its own words and credited generically.
Brief's claim of measurable physics holds for contrast and colour difference; spacing is partly perceptual and the lesson shows that honestly.
